/-!
# Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture

Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture (1973) asserts that, assuming the Riemann hypothesis,
the pair correlation between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function (normalized to have
unit average spacing) is
$$
  1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2,
$$
which, as Dyson pointed out to Montgomery, is the pair correlation function of the eigenvalues
of random Hermitian matrices (the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble).

Precisely: write the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ as $1/2 + i\gamma$ (this uses the Riemann
hypothesis). For fixed $\alpha \le \beta$, the conjecture states that
$$
  \lim_{T \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{(\gamma, \gamma') : 0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T \text{ and }
    2\pi\alpha/\log T \le \gamma - \gamma' \le 2\pi\beta/\log T\}}{\frac{T}{2\pi}\log T}
  = \int_\alpha^\beta \left(1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2\right)\,\mathrm{d}u
    + \delta(\alpha, \beta),
$$
where pairs of zeros are counted with multiplicity, $\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 1$ if
$0 \in [\alpha, \beta]$ and $\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 0$ otherwise.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery%27s_pair_correlation_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- H. L. Montgomery, *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, Analytic number theory
  (Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. XXIV, St. Louis Univ., St. Louis, Mo., 1972), Amer. Math. Soc.,
  Providence, R.I., 1973, pp. 181–193.
- E. Carneiro, V. Chandee, A. Chirre, M. B. Milinovich, *On Montgomery's pair correlation
  conjecture: a tale of three integrals*, [arXiv:2108.09258](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09258).
-/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def zeroMultiplicity (γ : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I)
blocks.docstring:
The multiplicity of the point $1/2 + i\gamma$ of the critical line as a zero of the Riemann
zeta function, i.e. the order of vanishing of $\zeta$ at $1/2 + i\gamma$. It is `0` when
$\zeta(1/2 + i\gamma) \ne 0$.

Under the Riemann hypothesis, the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ are exactly the points
$1/2 + i\gamma$ with `zeroMultiplicity γ ≠ 0`, and `zeroMultiplicity γ` is the multiplicity of
that zero.

justification.closest_existing_considered: analyticOrderAt / analyticOrderNatAt (Mathlib) — used directly; there is no Mathlib notion of 'multiplicity of a zero of riemannZeta' or of zero ordinates. Polynomial.rootMultiplicity and meromorphicOrderAt are not appropriate (ζ is analytic at these points).
justification.name: MontgomerysPairCorrelationConjecture.zeroMultiplicity
justification.why_needed: The conjecture counts zeros with multiplicity. Defined as analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1/2 + γ i), the order of vanishing of ζ at the critical-line point 1/2 + iγ (0 if not a zero). API lemmas in the file prove it is 0 iff ζ(1/2+iγ) ≠ 0 (positivity direction uses the identity theorem on ℂ \ {1} and ζ(2) ≠ 0, so the ⊤/junk case cannot occur).

blocks.docstring:
The set of ordered pairs $(\gamma, \gamma')$ of real numbers with $0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T$
and
$$
  \frac{2\pi\alpha}{\log T} \le \gamma - \gamma' \le \frac{2\pi\beta}{\log T}.
$$

justification.closest_existing_considered: Inline set-builder in the theorem statement; no Mathlib notion of zero ordinates of ζ or of pair sets of zeros exists.
justification.name: MontgomerysPairCorrelationConjecture.pairSet
justification.why_needed: The set of ordered pairs (ρ, ρ') ∈ ℂ × ℂ with 0 < Im ρ, Im ρ' ≤ T and 2πα/log T ≤ Im ρ − Im ρ' ≤ 2πβ/log T, i.e. the index set of Montgomery's double sum.

blocks.name: pairSet
blocks.text:
/-- The set of ordered pairs $(\gamma, \gamma')$ of real numbers with $0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T$
and
$$
  \frac{2\pi\alpha}{\log T} \le \gamma - \gamma' \le \frac{2\pi\beta}{\log T}.
$$ -/
def pairSet (α β T : ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ioc 0 T ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ioc 0 T ∧
    2 * π * α / Real.log T ≤ p.1 - p.2 ∧ p.1 - p.2 ≤ 2 * π * β / Real.log T}

blocks.code:
noncomputable def pairCount (α β T : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ᶠ p ∈ pairSet α β T, zeroMultiplicity p.1 * zeroMultiplicity p.2
blocks.docstring:
The number of ordered pairs $(\gamma, \gamma')$ of ordinates of zeros $1/2 + i\gamma$,
$1/2 + i\gamma'$ of the Riemann zeta function with $0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T$ and
$$
  \frac{2\pi\alpha}{\log T} \le \gamma - \gamma' \le \frac{2\pi\beta}{\log T},
$$
where each zero is counted with multiplicity, i.e. each pair $(\gamma, \gamma')$ is weighted by
the product of the multiplicities of $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$. Pairs with $\gamma = \gamma'$ are
included. The sum has finite support since $\zeta$ has only finitely many zeros with ordinate in
$(0, T]$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.ncard of a set of pairs — rejected because it cannot count with multiplicity; tsum — finsum is the standard repo idiom (EllipticCurveRank.lean) and cleaner.
justification.name: MontgomerysPairCorrelationConjecture.pairCount
justification.why_needed: The quantity N(α,β,T) = #{(γ,γ') : 0<γ,γ'≤T, 2πα/log T ≤ γ−γ' ≤ 2πβ/log T} with multiplicity. Defined as a finsum over the set of such ordered pairs (p : ℝ × ℝ) of zeroMultiplicity p.1 * zeroMultiplicity p.2. The support is finite (finitely many zeros on a compact segment), so the finsum is the true count; a test lemma checks pairCount = 0 for T ≤ 0.

blocks.name: pairCount
blocks.text:
/-- The number of ordered pairs $(\gamma, \gamma')$ of ordinates of zeros $1/2 + i\gamma$,
$1/2 + i\gamma'$ of the Riemann zeta function with $0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T$ and

blocks.code:
noncomputable def guePairCorrelation (u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 - Real.sinc (π * u) ^ 2
blocks.docstring:
The pair correlation function of the eigenvalues of random Hermitian matrices (the Gaussian
Unitary Ensemble), normalized to unit average spacing:
$$
  1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2.
$$
It is expressed with `Real.sinc`, so that its value at $u = 0$ is $0$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Real.sinc (Mathlib) — used as the building block; Mathlib has no GUE/sine-kernel pair correlation function.
justification.name: MontgomerysPairCorrelationConjecture.guePairCorrelation
justification.why_needed: The GUE pair correlation function 1 − (sin πu/(πu))^2, the 'random Hermitian matrices' side of the statement. Defined as 1 − Real.sinc (π u) ^ 2 so its value at u = 0 is the correct value 0 (rather than the junk 1 from 0/0 = 0). Test lemma checks guePairCorrelation 0 = 0.

blocks.name: guePairCorrelation
blocks.text:
/-- The pair correlation function of the eigenvalues of random Hermitian matrices (the Gaussian
Unitary Ensemble), normalized to unit average spacing:
$$
  1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2.

It is expressed with `Real.sinc`, so that its value at $u = 0$ is $0$. -/
noncomputable def guePairCorrelation (u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 - Real.sinc (π * u) ^ 2

@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem montgomerys_pair_correlation_conjecture (hRH : RiemannHypothesis) (α β : ℝ)
    (hαβ : α ≤ β) :
    Tendsto (fun T : ℝ => (pairCount α β T : ℝ) / (T / (2 * π) * Real.log T)) atTop
      (𝓝 ((∫ u in α..β, guePairCorrelation u) + if 0 ∈ Set.Icc α β then 1 else 0)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture.**

Assume the Riemann hypothesis, so that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are
$1/2 + i\gamma$ with $\gamma$ real. Let $\alpha \le \beta$ be fixed. Then
$$
  \lim_{T \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{(\gamma, \gamma') : 0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T \text{ and }
    2\pi\alpha/\log T \le \gamma - \gamma' \le 2\pi\beta/\log T\}}{\frac{T}{2\pi}\log T}
  = \int_\alpha^\beta \left(1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2\right)\,\mathrm{d}u
    + \delta(\alpha, \beta),
$$
where $\gamma, \gamma'$ run over the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ counted with
multiplicity, $\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 1$ if $0 \in [\alpha, \beta]$, and
$\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 0$ otherwise. That is, the normalized pair correlation function of the
zeros of $\zeta$ is the pair correlation function $1 - (\sin(\pi u) / (\pi u))^2$ of the
eigenvalues of random Hermitian matrices.

@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem zeroMultiplicity_pos_of_eq_zero {γ : ℝ}
    (h : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) = 0) : 0 < zeroMultiplicity γ := by
  have hs : (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I : ℂ) ≠ 1 := by
    intro hs
    have := congrArg Complex.re hs
    norm_num at this
  have hζ : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ riemannZeta {1}ᶜ :=
    DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd
      (fun z hz ↦ (differentiableAt_riemannZeta hz).differentiableWithinAt) isOpen_compl_singleton
  have han : AnalyticAt ℂ riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) := hζ _ hs
  have htop : analyticOrderAt riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) ≠ ⊤ := by
    intro htop
    rw [analyticOrderAt_eq_top] at htop
    have h2 := hζ.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero
      (isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank (Complex.rank_real_complex ▸ Nat.one_lt_ofNat)
        1).isPreconnected hs htop (show (2 : ℂ) ∈ {1}ᶜ by norm_num)
    exact riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re (s := 2) (by norm_num) h2
  unfold zeroMultiplicity analyticOrderNatAt
  rw [Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero, ne_eq, ENat.toNat_eq_zero, not_or, analyticOrderAt_eq_zero, not_or,
    not_not, not_not]
  exact ⟨⟨han, h⟩, htop⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem pairSet_eq_empty_of_lt {α β T : ℝ} (hT : 1 < T) (h : β < α) : pairSet α β T = ∅ := by
  have hlog : 0 < Real.log T := Real.log_pos hT
  ext p
  simp only [pairSet, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨-, -, h1, h2⟩
  have := (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hlog).mp (h1.trans h2)
  nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]

claims.decomposer_note: Precise form (article 'Conjecture' section; arXiv:2108.09258 statement (I)): assuming RH, for every fixed pair of reals α ≤ β, the count of ordered pairs (γ,γ') of zero ordinates (with multiplicity) in (0,T] with 2πα/log T ≤ γ−γ' ≤ 2πβ/log T, divided by (T/2π)·log T, tends as T→∞ to ∫_α^β (1−(sin πu/(πu))²) du + δ(α,β), where δ(α,β)=1 if 0∈[α,β] and 0 otherwise (the diagonal γ=γ' contribution); the 'random Hermitian matrices' side is the GUE kernel 1−(sin πu/(πu))², RH is an explicit hypothesis of the conjecture as stated (Wikipedia writes the zeros as 1/2+iγ), and the stronger F(α) conjecture, Odlyzko's numerics, and n-level/automorphic extensions in the article are not posed by the list entry.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same conjecture faithfully (Wikipedia 'Conjecture' section / Montgomery 1973): hypothesis RiemannHypothesis (Mathlib), fixed reals α ≤ β, ordered pairs of zero ordinates in (0,T] counted with multiplicity via analyticOrderNatAt, non-strict window 2πα/log T ≤ γ−γ' ≤ 2πβ/log T, normalisation (T/2π)·log T, real T → ∞ (atTop), limit ∫_α^β (1−(sin πu/πu)²) du + [0 ∈ [α,β]]. c06 chosen as base because it (i) models ordinates on the critical line exactly as the source writes zeros 1/2+iγ, (ii) uses Real.sinc so the GUE kernel has the correct value 0 at u=0 (c01/c04/c05 use sin/x with Lean's 0/0=0 junk at a single point — harmless for the integral but less clean), (iii) uses finsum (support is finite: finitely many zeros with ordinate in (0,T]) rather than the more exotic Sigma/Fin ncard encodings of c02/c03/c07, and (iv) ships proven API lemmas validating that zeroMultiplicity is 0 iff ζ(1/2+iγ) ≠ 0. Edits: factored the pair set into a named `pairSet` (c05 style), wrote δ as `if 0 ∈ Set.Icc α β then 1 else 0` mirroring the source (definitionally equal to c06's `α ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ β`), and added c01's test that the pair set is empty for β < α, T > 1 (explains why α ≤ β is needed).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture

Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture (1973) asserts that, assuming the Riemann hypothesis,
the pair correlation between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function (normalized to have
unit average spacing) is
$$
  1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2,
$$
which, as Dyson pointed out to Montgomery, is the pair correlation function of the eigenvalues
of random Hermitian matrices (the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble).

Precisely: write the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ as $1/2 + i\gamma$ (this uses the Riemann
hypothesis). For fixed $\alpha \le \beta$, the conjecture states that
$$
  \lim_{T \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{(\gamma, \gamma') : 0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T \text{ and }
    2\pi\alpha/\log T \le \gamma - \gamma' \le 2\pi\beta/\log T\}}{\frac{T}{2\pi}\log T}
  = \int_\alpha^\beta \left(1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2\right)\,\mathrm{d}u
    + \delta(\alpha, \beta),
$$
where pairs of zeros are counted with multiplicity, $\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 1$ if
$0 \in [\alpha, \beta]$ and $\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 0$ otherwise.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montgomery%27s_pair_correlation_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- H. L. Montgomery, *The pair correlation of zeros of the zeta function*, Analytic number theory
  (Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Vol. XXIV, St. Louis Univ., St. Louis, Mo., 1972), Amer. Math. Soc.,
  Providence, R.I., 1973, pp. 181–193.
- E. Carneiro, V. Chandee, A. Chirre, M. B. Milinovich, *On Montgomery's pair correlation
  conjecture: a tale of three integrals*, [arXiv:2108.09258](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09258).
-/

Under the Riemann hypothesis, the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ are exactly the points
$1/2 + i\gamma$ with `zeroMultiplicity γ ≠ 0`, and `zeroMultiplicity γ` is the multiplicity of
that zero. -/
noncomputable def zeroMultiplicity (γ : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I)

/-- The set of ordered pairs $(\gamma, \gamma')$ of real numbers with $0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T$
and
$$
  \frac{2\pi\alpha}{\log T} \le \gamma - \gamma' \le \frac{2\pi\beta}{\log T}.
$$ -/
def pairSet (α β T : ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ioc 0 T ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ioc 0 T ∧
    2 * π * α / Real.log T ≤ p.1 - p.2 ∧ p.1 - p.2 ≤ 2 * π * β / Real.log T}

/-- The number of ordered pairs $(\gamma, \gamma')$ of ordinates of zeros $1/2 + i\gamma$,
$1/2 + i\gamma'$ of the Riemann zeta function with $0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T$ and
$$
  \frac{2\pi\alpha}{\log T} \le \gamma - \gamma' \le \frac{2\pi\beta}{\log T},
$$
where each zero is counted with multiplicity, i.e. each pair $(\gamma, \gamma')$ is weighted by
the product of the multiplicities of $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$. Pairs with $\gamma = \gamma'$ are
included. The sum has finite support since $\zeta$ has only finitely many zeros with ordinate in
$(0, T]$. -/
noncomputable def pairCount (α β T : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ᶠ p ∈ pairSet α β T, zeroMultiplicity p.1 * zeroMultiplicity p.2

/-- The pair correlation function of the eigenvalues of random Hermitian matrices (the Gaussian
Unitary Ensemble), normalized to unit average spacing:
$$
  1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2.
$$
It is expressed with `Real.sinc`, so that its value at $u = 0$ is $0$. -/
noncomputable def guePairCorrelation (u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 - Real.sinc (π * u) ^ 2

/-- **Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture.**

Assume the Riemann hypothesis, so that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are
$1/2 + i\gamma$ with $\gamma$ real. Let $\alpha \le \beta$ be fixed. Then
$$
  \lim_{T \to \infty}
  \frac{\#\{(\gamma, \gamma') : 0 < \gamma, \gamma' \le T \text{ and }
    2\pi\alpha/\log T \le \gamma - \gamma' \le 2\pi\beta/\log T\}}{\frac{T}{2\pi}\log T}
  = \int_\alpha^\beta \left(1 - \left(\frac{\sin(\pi u)}{\pi u}\right)^2\right)\,\mathrm{d}u
    + \delta(\alpha, \beta),
$$
where $\gamma, \gamma'$ run over the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ counted with
multiplicity, $\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 1$ if $0 \in [\alpha, \beta]$, and
$\delta(\alpha, \beta) = 0$ otherwise. That is, the normalized pair correlation function of the
zeros of $\zeta$ is the pair correlation function $1 - (\sin(\pi u) / (\pi u))^2$ of the
eigenvalues of random Hermitian matrices. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem montgomerys_pair_correlation_conjecture (hRH : RiemannHypothesis) (α β : ℝ)
    (hαβ : α ≤ β) :
    Tendsto (fun T : ℝ => (pairCount α β T : ℝ) / (T / (2 * π) * Real.log T)) atTop
      (𝓝 ((∫ u in α..β, guePairCorrelation u) + if 0 ∈ Set.Icc α β then 1 else 0)) := by
  sorry

/-- If $\zeta(1/2 + i\gamma) \ne 0$ then $1/2 + i\gamma$ has multiplicity `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem zeroMultiplicity_eq_zero_of_ne_zero {γ : ℝ}
    (h : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) ≠ 0) : zeroMultiplicity γ = 0 := by
  unfold zeroMultiplicity analyticOrderNatAt
  rw [analyticOrderAt_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inr h), ENat.toNat_zero]

/-- If $\zeta(1/2 + i\gamma) = 0$ then $1/2 + i\gamma$ has positive multiplicity. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem zeroMultiplicity_pos_of_eq_zero {γ : ℝ}
    (h : riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) = 0) : 0 < zeroMultiplicity γ := by
  have hs : (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I : ℂ) ≠ 1 := by
    intro hs
    have := congrArg Complex.re hs
    norm_num at this
  have hζ : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ riemannZeta {1}ᶜ :=
    DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd
      (fun z hz ↦ (differentiableAt_riemannZeta hz).differentiableWithinAt) isOpen_compl_singleton
  have han : AnalyticAt ℂ riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) := hζ _ hs
  have htop : analyticOrderAt riemannZeta (1 / 2 + γ * Complex.I) ≠ ⊤ := by
    intro htop
    rw [analyticOrderAt_eq_top] at htop
    have h2 := hζ.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq_zero
      (isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank (Complex.rank_real_complex ▸ Nat.one_lt_ofNat)
        1).isPreconnected hs htop (show (2 : ℂ) ∈ {1}ᶜ by norm_num)
    exact riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re (s := 2) (by norm_num) h2
  unfold zeroMultiplicity analyticOrderNatAt
  rw [Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero, ne_eq, ENat.toNat_eq_zero, not_or, analyticOrderAt_eq_zero, not_or,
    not_not, not_not]
  exact ⟨⟨han, h⟩, htop⟩

/-- There are no pairs to count when `T ≤ 0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem pairSet_eq_empty_of_nonpos {α β T : ℝ} (hT : T ≤ 0) : pairSet α β T = ∅ := by
  ext p
  simp only [pairSet, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_Ioc, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, -⟩
  linarith

/-- There are no pairs of zeros to count when `T ≤ 0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem pairCount_of_nonpos {α β T : ℝ} (hT : T ≤ 0) : pairCount α β T = 0 := by
  rw [pairCount, pairSet_eq_empty_of_nonpos hT, finsum_mem_empty]

/-- If $\beta < \alpha$ and $T > 1$ then no pair $(\gamma, \gamma')$ satisfies the constraints. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem pairSet_eq_empty_of_lt {α β T : ℝ} (hT : 1 < T) (h : β < α) : pairSet α β T = ∅ := by
  have hlog : 0 < Real.log T := Real.log_pos hT
  ext p
  simp only [pairSet, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  rintro ⟨-, -, h1, h2⟩
  have := (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hlog).mp (h1.trans h2)
  nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]

/-- The GUE pair correlation function vanishes at `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem guePairCorrelation_zero : guePairCorrelation 0 = 0 := by
  simp [guePairCorrelation]

end MontgomerysPairCorrelationConjecture

items: RH is taken as an explicit hypothesis (hRH : RiemannHypothesis) of the theorem, following the Wikipedia 'Conjecture' section ('Under the assumption that the Riemann hypothesis is true') and the decomposition notes. Consequently zero ordinates are read off the critical line: γ is an ordinate iff ζ(1/2 + iγ) = 0. Under RH this is exactly the set of ordinates of non-trivial zeros; without RH the statement is vacuous, as is standard for 'assuming RH' statements in the repo (e.g. Wikipedia/Mills.lean).

Pairs are counted with multiplicity (weight m(γ)·m(γ') for ordered pairs of distinct ordinates, diagonal pairs included), following Montgomery's convention, the decomposition notes and arXiv:2108.09258 ('counted with multiplicity'). With this convention and δ(α,β)=1 the conjecture also encodes that almost all zeros are simple, as in Montgomery's original paper. Wikipedia's set-builder notation #{(γ,γ')} could be read as counting distinct pairs; I followed the explicit 'with multiplicity' reading of the notes.

The count is a finsum over ℝ × ℝ; finsum returns 0 on infinite support, but the support (pairs of zeros in (0,T]²) is finite because ζ is analytic and not identically zero on a neighbourhood of the compact segment {1/2 + iγ : γ ∈ [0,T]}, so no junk value is reachable.

Both window bounds are non-strict (≤ ... ≤), γ, γ' ∈ (0, T] (Set.Ioc 0 T), the normalisation is (T/(2π))·log T, and T → ∞ is Filter.atTop over ℝ, all exactly as in the Wikipedia formula. For T ≤ 1 the expression 2πα/log T is degenerate (log T ≤ 0, division by 0 at T = 1) but this is irrelevant to the limit at atTop.
δ(α,β) is encoded as `if α ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ β then 1 else 0`, i.e. 1 iff 0 ∈ [α, β].

The hypothesis α ≤ β is kept: for α > β the window is eventually empty so the LHS tends to 0 while the RHS is negative, so the statement would be false without it; the source says 'Let α ≤ β be fixed'.

The integral is the Mathlib interval integral ∫ u in α..β; the GUE kernel uses Real.sinc so that the integrand equals 1 − (sin πu/(πu))² everywhere including u = 0 (where it is 0). Stronger/other forms in the article (Montgomery's F(α) conjecture, Odlyzko's spacing statistics, n-level correlations, automorphic L-functions) are not stated, per the decomposition notes.

reviewer_notes: The list entry is one informal sentence; all candidates and the final file use the precise limit form from the Wikipedia article's 'Conjecture' section, which matches Montgomery's 1973 statement and the decomposition notes. Modeling points a human should be aware of: (1) RH is an explicit hypothesis, and ordinates are read off the critical line (ζ(1/2+iγ)=0) — under RH this equals the set of non-trivial zero ordinates; c01/c04 instead sum over all complex zeros with imaginary part in (0,T] / in the strip, which is equivalent under RH and also fine, but the critical-line form mirrors the source text. (2) Pairs are counted with multiplicity (weight m_γ·m_γ'), per the decomposition notes and Montgomery's convention; with the δ term this encodes that almost all zeros are simple, as in the original conjecture. Wikipedia's set-builder notation could be misread as counting distinct pairs, but the notes explicitly request multiplicity. (3) finsum returns 0 on infinite support, but the support is finite for every T (finitely many zeros with ordinate ≤ T), so no junk value is reachable. (4) For T ≤ 1, log T ≤ 0 gives degenerate window bounds/normalisation, irrelevant for the atTop limit. (5) α ≤ β is required (for β < α the count is eventually 0 while the integral is negative); α = β cases follow from α < β by monotonicity so the ≤ form of Wikipedia is equivalent to Montgomery's < form. No candidate omitted the slot; all compiled with only the sorry warning.
statement: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture: the normalized pair correlation function between pairs of zeros of the Riemann zeta function is the same as the pair correlation function of random Hermitian matrices.
